title: Flora's Sparkly Hat Rescue
markdown:
The sun burst through Madoc the squirrel’s window like a golden trumpet call. Bright yellow stripes poked into his cozy oak-tree nest and kicked off the morning. “Wow!” he chirped. His whiskers wiggled with happiness. The air smelled fresh, like damp earth and a day that wanted to begin. Today felt special. He just knew it.

He practically bounced down the trunk, bushy tail a blur of brown. He could not wait to greet his very best pal, Flora the duckling. But when he got to the stream, Flora sat alone. She looked very sad. Her fluffy yellow feathers drooped. They looked like sad flowers.

“Flora! What’s up?” Madoc landed with a soft thump.

She let out a tiny shaky sigh. “Oh, Madoc. My hat. My favourite hat! The one with the sparkly blue ribbon that caught the sun. A big gusty wind — whoosh! — blew it right away.”

Madoc’s tail puffed. “Don’t you worry one bit. We’ll get it back. A mission!” His sharp eyes found their little red-and-white toy boat, bobbing by the reeds. “This is perfect.”

“A boat?” Flora’s feet shuffled. “The stream is so splashy and swooshy.” She felt wobbly about fast water.

“We’ll paddle together! A grand hat rescue!”

They climbed in with care. Madoc took a sturdy twig. Flora sat in front, peeking downstream, hopeful and a little worried. “Ready?” She nodded, chest puffed.

“Go!” she quacked, squeaky and brave.

Whoosh! The swift current instantly grabbed their little boat. It zoomed downstream like a shooting star. The water chuckled and gurgled, a bubbly happy sound. Madoc paddled with all his might, little paws working fast. “Wheee!” His eyes were wide. A real adventure was happening.

Suddenly a big bumpy log, covered in moss, blocked their path. “Uh oh!” Flora squeaked. Her little body tensed.

“Quick! Duck! Paddle left! Hard left!” Madoc’s brain worked super fast. They zipped around the log. The boat wobbled a lot for a split second. Flora wobbled too, webbed feet flailing for balance, but she bravely stayed put. That took a lot of staying.

Around the bend, a grumpy frog sat on a lily pad. He blinked slowly. “Ribbit. What are you two doing, disturbing my nap?”

Madoc grinned. “A super important hat rescue, Mr. Frog.”

The frog’s golden eyes considered. “A hat? Hmm. I haven’t seen any sparkly hats. Just lots of bubbly water.” A sticky toe pointed downstream. “Keep paddling. Don’t dawdle.”

“Thank you kindly!” They paddled faster. Madoc remembered Grandpa Squirrel: on an adventure, eyes wide, paws ready.

Then Flora gasped. “Madoc! Look!”

Snagged on a low green branch that dipped its leafy fingers toward the water — a dazzling flash of blue. The ribbon fluttered like a tiny flag. “We found it!” She jumped; the boat nearly tipped.

Madoc steered closer. The branch was just too far. Flora’s tummy did a flip. Reaching over water was a bit scary. The hat was so close.

“I can do it!” She stretched her neck. She spread her wings for balance. Wiggle, wiggle. Reach, reach. Pop! Her beak snagged the ribbon. She pulled, legs braced.

There it was. The sparkly blue hat, slightly damp, perfectly hers.

“Hooray for Flora!” Madoc did a little jig. Flora beamed and set the hat on her head. It sparkled in the morning sun. “We did it!”

They paddled back. The boat bobbed as if it knew the job was done. The stream’s chuckle sounded like a song. They jumped to shore.

Flora adjusted the ribbon. She was not even that nervous, not really — or so she told the hat, which did not argue. They raced off along the bank, hat flashing, twig paddle left for another day, the water still going whoosh behind them like a friend who had given the current back.
